memory_update.text: AXTI is the clearest primary chokepoint name in this chunk because its revenue and shipments are tied to InP substrate export permits, making it both demand-exposed and policy-constrained.
CAMT and KLIC sit one step downstream of the HBM story and should be treated as equipment/inspection leverage rather than raw-material bottlenecks.
ALM, KMT, and ELMT form a separate tungsten-critical-minerals cluster; ALM is the cleaner upstream supply expression, while KMT and ELMT are downstream conversion / component names.
POWL belongs to the AI power buildout lane and should not be conflated with semiconductor or materials bottlenecks.
TGB, ECVT, and HWKN are second-order sulphuric-acid chain exposures; the main falsification risk is that they benefit only transiently or not at all if feedstock pricing normalizes.
Need primary-source verification from filings, earnings calls, investor presentations, and government export-control documents before promoting any narrative proxy to a durable thesis.

summary: Candidate chunk maps to two main underfollowed chokepoint lanes inside New Hotspots: AI optical interconnect substrates and HBM/advanced-packaging inspection and assembly. A third lane captures sulphuric-acid disruption feeding copper SX-EW / nickel HPAL, and a fourth lane captures tungsten / refractory-metals supply for defense and hardmetals. Within this chunk, AXTI is the most direct underfollowed bottleneck expression; CAMT and KLIC are the clearest adjacent equipment beneficiaries; ALM, KMT, and ELMT are the most direct non-AI critical-minerals expressions; POWL is a separate AI power-infrastructure implementation layer; TGB and ECVT/HWKN are more second-order acid-chain exposures. The main unresolved question is whether each name is a true revenue beneficiary of the bottleneck or only a narrative proxy.
